input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called? It’s been a few hours now and they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.
Yes, it’s the number I gave you—555-123-2002—that’s having the problem. What should I do next?

It looks like my phone’s status bar is showing the airplane icon, and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see anything about signal strength or mobile data. Does that mean airplane mode is on? What should I do?

Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see something that looks like “no signal” and it says data is disabled. I’m not sure what to do next—should I try sending a picture message now, or is there something else I need to check?
It looks like my phone is saying there’s no SIM card detected. What does that mean? Is that why I can’t send picture messages? What should I do now?

Alright, I’ve taken out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now my phone shows a signal, but it says “2G” and data is still disabled. Is that good enough to send a picture message, or do I need to do something else?

I’ve turned on mobile data, but my phone still says “2G” and the signal is poor. Should I try sending a picture message now, or do I need to do something else to get a better connection? I’m not sure how to change the network type.

Okay, I changed the network mode like you said, and now my phone shows an excellent signal and says “5G” with data enabled. Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there anything else I need to check first?
I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. It looks like my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. What should I do now? This is getting a bit frustrating.

I found the option to reset the APN settings, and it says they’ll reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit nervous—if I reboot my phone, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Can you reassure me before I do this?

My phone has restarted and everything looks the same—signal is excellent, 5G is showing, and data is enabled. But I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried this won’t get fixed.

I checked and Wi-Fi Calling was turned on, so I’ve switched it off now. Also, it looks like my messaging app only has permission for the phone, not for storage or SMS. Should I enable those permissions too before trying to send a picture message again?
I’ve enabled both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really hoping we can get this working soon.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hello, I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called? It’s been a few hours now and they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?

I can help you troubleshoot your MMS (picture messaging) issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Thank you for providing your information, John. I’ll help you troubleshoot your MMS issue.

To begin, could you confirm which phone number (if you have more than one line) is having trouble sending picture messages? If it’s the number you provided (555-123-2002), please let me know, and I’ll guide you through some quick checks on your device to identify the problem.
Yes, it’s the number I gave you—555-123-2002—that’s having the problem. What should I do next?

Thank you for confirming. Let’s start by checking a few things on your device to diagnose the MMS issue.

First, please check your phone’s status bar and let me know what you see regarding:
- Signal strength (bars or signal icon)
- Network type (e.g., 4G, 5G, LTE, 3G, E, etc.)
- Airplane mode (is it on or off?)
- Mobile data (is it enabled or disabled?)

This information will help determine if there are any basic connectivity issues affecting MMS. Please describe what you see, or if you’re able to, use your phone’s diagnostic feature to check the status bar and share the results.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%

It looks like my phone’s status bar is showing the airplane icon, and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see anything about signal strength or mobile data. Does that mean airplane mode is on? What should I do?

Yes, if you see the airplane icon in your status bar, that means Airplane Mode is currently ON. When Airplane Mode is enabled, all wireless communications—including cellular service and mobile data—are turned off, which will prevent you from sending or receiving MMS messages.

To fix this:
1. Please turn OFF Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings panel and tapping the airplane icon, or by going to your phone’s settings and toggling Airplane Mode off.
2. Once Airplane Mode is off, wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect to the cellular network. You should see signal bars and your network type (like 4G or 5G) reappear in the status bar.

After you’ve done this, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you still have trouble, and we’ll continue troubleshooting if needed.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see something that looks like “no signal” and it says data is disabled. I’m not sure what to do next—should I try sending a picture message now, or is there something else I need to check?

Since your phone now shows “no signal” and data is disabled, you won’t be able to send MMS yet. Let’s address these issues step by step:

1. First, let’s check your SIM card status to make sure your phone is recognizing it correctly.
2. Next, we’ll make sure mobile data is enabled, since MMS requires an active data connection.

Could you please check your SIM card status on your phone? Look for any messages about the SIM being missing, locked, or inactive. If you’re not sure how to check, let me know what you see in your notifications or settings related to the SIM card.

Once you’ve checked, please let me know what it says, and we’ll continue from there.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
It looks like my phone is saying there’s no SIM card detected. What does that mean? Is that why I can’t send picture messages? What should I do now?

If your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, that is likely the reason you can’t send picture messages (MMS) or use cellular service. The SIM card is required for your phone to connect to the network.

Here’s what you should do:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Remove the SIM card from its slot.
3. Carefully reinsert the SIM card, making sure it’s properly seated.
4. Power your phone back on.

After your phone restarts, check if the SIM card is now detected (you should see signal bars or your carrier’s name in the status bar). If you see the SIM card is recognized, try sending a picture message again.

If your phone still says there’s no SIM card detected after reseating it, please let me know, and we’ll look into further steps.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I’ve taken out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now my phone shows a signal, but it says “2G” and data is still disabled. Is that good enough to send a picture message, or do I need to do something else?

A “2G” connection is generally not sufficient for sending picture messages (MMS), and mobile data must be enabled for MMS to work. Here’s what you should do next:

1. Enable mobile data on your phone. You can usually do this by swiping down from the top of your screen and tapping the mobile data icon, or by going to your phone’s settings and turning on mobile data.
2. After enabling mobile data, check if your phone connects to a higher network type (like 3G, 4G, or 5G). If it still shows “2G,” you’ll need to change your network mode preference to allow faster connections.

Please enable mobile data and let me know:
- If you’re able to switch to 3G, 4G, or 5G,
- Or if it still stays on 2G.

Once you have mobile data enabled and a higher network type, try sending a picture message again. If you need help changing your network mode, let me know and I’ll guide you through it.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I’ve turned on mobile data, but my phone still says “2G” and the signal is poor. Should I try sending a picture message now, or do I need to do something else to get a better connection? I’m not sure how to change the network type.

A “2G” connection is usually too slow for sending picture messages (MMS). To improve your connection, you should change your phone’s network mode preference to allow 3G, 4G, or 5G if available.

Here’s what you need to do:
- Go to your phone’s settings.
- Find the section for “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
- Look for “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
- Select an option like “4G/3G/2G (auto connect)” or “5G/4G/3G/2G (auto connect)” if available.

After changing the network mode, wait a moment to see if your phone connects to a higher network type (like 3G, 4G, or 5G). Once you see a better connection, try sending a picture message again.

If you’re not sure how to find these settings, let me know your phone’s make and model, and I can provide more specific instructions.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I changed the network mode like you said, and now my phone shows an excellent signal and says “5G” with data enabled. Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there anything else I need to check first?

That’s great progress! With an excellent signal, “5G” network, and data enabled, your phone now meets the requirements for sending picture messages (MMS).

Please try sending a picture message now. If it goes through successfully, your issue is resolved. If you still have trouble sending MMS, let me know, and we’ll check a few more settings to ensure everything is configured correctly.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. It looks like my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. What should I do now? This is getting a bit frustrating.

Thank you for your patience. Since you now have a strong signal and data enabled, but MMS still isn’t working, the next most common cause is incorrect APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for MMS.

Here’s what you should do:
1. Go to your phone’s settings.
2. Find the section for “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
3. Look for “Access Point Names” (APN).
4. Check if there’s an option to “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.” Select this option to reset your APN settings to the carrier defaults.

After resetting your APN settings, you must reboot your phone for the changes to take effect:
- Power off your phone, wait a few seconds, and then power it back on.

Once your phone restarts, try sending a picture message again.

If you need step-by-step instructions for your specific phone model, let me know. If MMS still doesn’t work after these steps, please tell me what error message (if any) you see when trying to send a picture message.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I found the option to reset the APN settings, and it says they’ll reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit nervous—if I reboot my phone, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Can you reassure me before I do this?

Rebooting your phone (simply turning it off and then back on) will not delete any of your photos, messages, or other personal data. It’s a safe process that just refreshes your phone’s system and applies any new settings, such as the APN changes you just made.

You can go ahead and restart your phone with confidence. Once it powers back on, try sending a picture message again. If you have any issues after the reboot, let me know and I’ll continue to help you.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

My phone has restarted and everything looks the same—signal is excellent, 5G is showing, and data is enabled. But I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried this won’t get fixed.

Thank you for letting me know. I understand this is frustrating, but there are still a few more things we can check to resolve your MMS issue.

Let’s try the following steps:

1. **Check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled:** Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS. Please check your phone’s settings for “Wi-Fi Calling.” If it’s ON, try turning it OFF and then attempt to send a picture message again.

2. **Check messaging app permissions:** Your messaging app needs permission to access storage and SMS. Go to your phone’s settings, find “Apps” or “Applications,” select your messaging app, and check its permissions. Make sure “Storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled.

Please try these steps and let me know:
- If Wi-Fi Calling was on and you turned it off,
- If you had to enable any permissions for your messaging app,
- And if you’re able to send a picture message after making these changes.

If it still doesn’t work, let me know what happens or if you see any error messages. I’m here to help until we get this resolved!

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.

I checked and Wi-Fi Calling was turned on, so I’ve switched it off now. Also, it looks like my messaging app only has permission for the phone, not for storage or SMS. Should I enable those permissions too before trying to send a picture message again?

Yes, please enable both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions for your messaging app. These permissions are required for sending and receiving picture messages (MMS):

- “Storage” permission allows the app to access your photos and media files.
- “SMS” permission allows the app to send and receive messages.

After enabling these permissions, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you still encounter any issues.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.

Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I’ve enabled both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really hoping we can get this working soon.

Thank you for following all the steps so far. Since you have:
- Excellent signal and 5G data enabled,
- Reset your APN settings and rebooted,
- Disabled Wi-Fi Calling,
- Enabled storage and SMS permissions for your messaging app,

and you still cannot send MMS, we have covered all standard troubleshooting steps.

At this point, your issue may require advanced technical support or a deeper account/system check that I am unable to perform directly. I will transfer you to a human agent who can further investigate and resolve your MMS issue.
